items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...because it predated, say, Wayne Shorter's entry.

ctx.x: -- Bill Holman did for the band. Yeah, that's the suite. (unintelligible)

Right, and that actually has some, I think, some significance to the development of the use of the soprano saxophone in a wider way of the last ten years or more, because it predated, say, Wayne Shorter's entry.

Yeah, well, I think that it was one of the first people to really want to take a shot at it, like, the people of my ilk, at least. And when I heard John do it, -- and John and I had some very meaningful talks on occasion, that never lasted very long. But he could never understand why I did what I did, and I guess I stated the same case as far as he was concerned.
